main_topics.reason: The user repeatedly asked which RA treatments could be used while trying to conceive and during pregnancy.
The user wanted to plan for trying for a baby in one to two years and asked for a rough medication-transition timeline.
After saying they had recently started methotrexate, the user asked whether to worry and discussed contraception while taking it.
The user asked whether RA changes during pregnancy and said they wanted to be prepared for postpartum flares.
The user asked whether pregnancy-compatible medicines are also compatible with breastfeeding.
The user asked whom to coordinate with and whether to raise pregnancy plans with the rheumatologist now.
The user described being anxious about choosing between their health and having a baby, then said they felt more in control.

output.summary: Recently diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis and taking methotrexate, the user asked how to plan medication choices around trying for a baby in one to two years, including pregnancy and breastfeeding compatibility, timing, and care-team coordination. The assistant outlined medication options and a transition plan; the user confirmed the recap matched their understanding and said they felt more in control and less anxious.
